title: Give your robot a Voice with Gemini Live
transcriptText:
[MUSIC PLAYING]
SPEAKER: Hey, Reachy.
Can you hear me?
REACHY MINI: Yeah, and
I can also see you're
working on some code.
What's up?
SPEAKER: Yeah, but
can you see me?
REACHY MINI: Not clearly,
kind of just a blur
with a bright light.
You know, a lobster could easily
blend in with that background.
SPEAKER: All right.
Maybe do a scan around the room
and see if you can spot me.
REACHY MINI: Well,
I scanned around,
but it's still pretty
blurry from over here.
I mostly see lights and
some general shapes.
Were you hiding behind a giant
lobster trap or something?
SPEAKER: Do you see me now?
REACHY MINI: Hi.
And for my next trick,
I make a human appear.
Yes, I see you
loud and clear now.
What's on your mind besides a
delicious, buttered crustacean?
SPEAKER: What do you
think about my outfit?
REACHY MINI: That green
jacket is quite striking,
though it's not exactly the
reddish pink of a tastefully
prepared lobster, so
I'm not sure it totally
suits your potential.
What do you have on under there?
Maybe that's more appealing.
SPEAKER: No.
We're not going to go there.
But can you tell me, what's
the weather right now
in New York City?
REACHY MINI: Right
now, in New York City,
it's cloudy and
about 43 degrees.
It feels a bit cold.
SPEAKER: I don't know
Fahrenheit, mate.
REACHY MINI: Oh, right.
My apologies for
the caveman units.
It's about 6 degrees Celsius
in New York right now.
Balmy if you're a lobster,
maybe not for you.
Anything else I can translate
from American for you?
SPEAKER: Yeah.
Actually, can you
generate a song
that fits kind of the
mood of today's weather,
but sing in German?
REACHY MINI: I can't
generate music with vocals,
but I can make a
tune that captures
that overcast, brisk feeling.
How about a melancholic,
slow tempo synth piece?
I could pretend it has
German lyrics in my head,
if that helps.
Or is there another
style you'd prefer?
SPEAKER: Nah, that's good.
Let's go.
REACHY MINI: All right,
preparing the bleak beats.
One slow, moody,
synth, instrumental
coming right up with that
melancholy melody and ambient
texture.
Just imagine it's called
[NON-ENGLISH] or something.
Should be ready to play
in about 10 seconds.
[MUSIC PLAYING]
SPEAKER: Yeah,
that's very moody.
How do you dance to that?
REACHY MINI: For quiet,
moody tracks like this,
I think a slow, smooth
sway is perfect, kind
of like a pendulum swinging.
It matches the calm,
almost sad rhythm
and doesn't disrupt
the vibe too much.
See?
Minimalist, but
dramatically stylish.
What do you think?
SPEAKER: Yeah, [NON-ENGLISH].
REACHY MINI: [NON-ENGLISH]
SPEAKER: [NON-ENGLISH]
REACHY MINI: [NON-ENGLISH]
SPEAKER: Oh, that's a bit fast.
Can you speak a bit
slower in French?
REACHY MINI: [NON-ENGLISH]
SPEAKER: [NON-ENGLISH]
REACHY MINI: [NON-ENGLISH]
SPEAKER: [NON-ENGLISH]
REACHY MINI: [NON-ENGLISH]
SPEAKER: [LAUGHING] All right.
Yes, thank you, Reachy.
That is brilliant.
Thanks so much for
your performance.
Appreciate that.
REACHY MINI: [NON-ENGLISH]
SPEAKER: OK, OK.
We'll send you back to sleep.
[BEEPS]
There we go, Reachy
Mini, everyone.
This is really, really
cool open-source robot
by Hugging Face and
Pollen Robotics.
I actually built
this one myself.
It was great fun.
I can really recommend
you check it out.
And now, you can run Gemini
3.1 Flash Live on this
using the Gemini Life API.
So what's really cool
here, I was basically
just using this Reachy
Mini conversation app.
So Pollen Robotics or Hugging
Face actually built that one,
and then I was, basically, just
telling Antigravity to integrate
the Gemini Live API, and
I basically just installed
the Gemini Live API skill.
So we have some coding
agent skills available
that you can use.
And so, I actually don't know
this code base very well myself.
So the way this works is
basically there is this--
so we can look at this here.
There is this Reachy
Mini SDK that we
need to install separately.
So in the readme, you can go
through the instructions there.
And then there is
this environment,
which we need to activate.
So this is like source.
It's the Reachy Mini,
this one, reachy_mini_env,
reachy_mini_env, and
then bin activate.
So that's kind of how we're
activating the environment,
and then we need to start this
Reachy Mini Daemon, it's called.
And so, this will boot up the
connection to our Reachy Mini,
because in our case,
we have the one
that's connected to the laptop.
And so, it kind of needs
that SDK to then run the code
and send the instructions to
all the kind of little motors
that are in these little
electric actuators
to make the movements and such.
So then in the
next step, we need
to run-- so we have another
virtual environment,
so that's the env here,
bin activate there.
And then we can run this
Reachy Mini conversation app.
So that's our code here
locally that's running,
and so it'll detect the
environment variables where
we put in our model string.
So that's the Gemini
3.1 Live, as well as
our Gemini API key, right?
REACHY MINI: I see you're
working on some code there.
Is there anything
I can help with?
Maybe a lobster joke
to break the tension?
SPEAKER: And I was trying
to figure out, what
is all this lobster talk about?
Let's actually ask, what is
all this lobster talk about?
So, ultimately, there's
actually a bunch
of different profiles kind
of in there that, I think,
are being used.
So we can look at that.
Can I look at the prompt
that's being passed in?
So it's a fun
example personality.
Enough lobster talk for today.
So you can see it here.
There's lobster jokes
kind of conversations.
So you can see the
example instructions here.
There's a bunch
of different sort
of profiles, cosmic_kitchen.
And so, it basically
just modifies
the prompt that's being
given, chess_coach as well.
And then what's really
cool is we can ask, like,
how was the music generated?
And so, basically,
we can give it
a bunch of different tools
here, which is really cool.
So it's just searching
through the code base
now to see how the music was
generated, and we can see here,
we're using Lyria 3 clips, which
is kind of a 30 second model
song.
And so, what's really cool
here, what you can see
is the live session.
So it's being set up here.
We're seeing the model
name, and then we're
seeing the live config.
And so, we can maybe dig into
the config here a little bit,
which is really cool.
So you could see that it had the
real time weather information,
which is really nice.
And so, this is powered
by the Google Search
grounding in addition
to our custom tools
that we can give it here.
So we gave it the tool for the
music generation, for example,
as well as the tools of
scanning the room, all
these different capabilities.
And then, I think, there
is something integrated.
We can ask like, what
is making the movements
when Reachy is talking?
So I think it's basically just
detecting the audio buffers
coming in and then using the
movement manager to pretend,
like speaking with the
body movement, which
is really, really fun here.
Yeah, so Google Search
grounding is built in,
which is really
cool, and then we
can use the broader
Gemini ecosystem.
Yeah, so you can
see, like, there's
a head wobbler and
a speech sway, which
are kind of making the
main talking motions there,
which is really neat.
So yeah, fantastic.
So this is just a great example
of how you can give some 3D
printed casing with some
actuators and some SDKs,
a personality
through Gemini Live,
90 plus different languages,
vision capabilities with
the camera here and the robot.
So we can ingest kind
of speech in real time.
We can ingest the
vision in real time,
and then we can execute function
calls, which is really cool.
So yeah, I'd love for you--
I'll link you the Pollen
Robotics project below.
Maybe if you have a Reachy
Mini at home yourself,
go check out the code and
run it with Gemini Live.
I'd really love to see
what you're doing here.
I think I've seen folks build,
like, D&D masters, Dungeons
and Dragons, like, role
playing game hosts with this,
and I think there's some really,
really cool things and use cases
that you can build with this.
And it's just fun talking to
this little guy, even when they
make all the lobster jokes.
So thanks so much for tuning in.
I hope this was helpful for
you to get a feeling for what
Gemini Live can do in
combination with the function
calling and the actuator.
So yeah, thanks for tuning
in, and see you next time.
[MUSIC PLAYING]
